name: Tree View
description: A hierarchical list where parent items can be expanded and collapsed to show or hide child items, supporting single-select and multi-select modes.

keyboard_interactions.action: Opens closed node; moves to first child on open node; no-op on end node
Closes open node; moves to parent from child node
Moves focus to next visible node
Moves focus to previous visible node
Moves focus to last visible node
Moves focus to node matching typed character(s)
(Optional) Expands all sibling nodes at current level

required_attributes.description: true when open; false when closed; omit on end nodes

optional_attributes.description: true on selected nodes; false on unselected
Number of siblings at this level

notes: Ask first whether you need a tree. A navigation sidebar with expandable sections is usually a <nav> containing nested <ul>s with disclosure buttons — far simpler, and it keeps normal link semantics.
role='tree' switches screen readers into application mode: normal reading keys stop working and the user must know the tree keyboard model. That is a real cost.
One Tab stop, roving tabindex. Right expands (or moves to the first child), Left collapses (or moves to the parent), Up/Down move through VISIBLE items only — not through collapsed children.

aria-level, aria-setsize and aria-posinset are required when the DOM structure does not express the nesting (a flattened tree). With genuinely nested <ul>/role='group' the browser computes level for you.
aria-expanded goes only on items that HAVE children. A leaf with aria-expanded='false' claims children it does not have.
Type-ahead is expected: typing a letter jumps to the next visible item starting with it.
Collapsed branches must be `hidden` or removed from the DOM (RAWeb 10.8).
native_element: none — nested <ul> with <a> is a better fit for a site tree or file listing

raweb_criteria.reason: aria-expanded, aria-level, aria-selected and the tree/treeitem roles must all be exposed — nothing here is native.
Arrows navigate and expand/collapse; the whole widget must be keyboard operable.
The focused item must be visibly indicated as focus roves.
Collapsed branches must be hidden from assistive technologies, not just visually.
Roving tabindex keeps the tree a single Tab stop.
Tab must leave the tree — arrows navigate within it.
